items.stem: State any three contents of a partnership deed.
items.answer: Names and addresses of the firm and partners; Nature of business; Capital contributed by each partner; Profit-sharing ratio; Interest on capital and drawings; Salary or commission to partners; Rules for admission, retirement and death; Method of settling disputes
items.markingKey: Any three of: Names and addresses of the firm and partners; Nature of business; Capital contributed by each partner; Profit-sharing ratio; Interest on capital and drawings; Salary or commission to partners; Rules for admission, retirement and death; Method of settling disputes (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the provisions applicable in the absence of a partnership deed is correct?
items.answer: No partner is entitled to a salary.
items.markingKey: (b) Correct: No partner is entitled to a salary.
options: Interest on capital is allowed at 6% per annum.
No partner is entitled to a salary.
Profits are shared in the capital ratio.
Interest on a partner's loan is allowed at 12% per annum.

items.stem: Explain the following provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 that apply in the absence of a partnership deed: (i) Interest on a partner's loan at 6% per annum (ii) No salary or commission to any partner.
items.answer: (i) Interest on a partner's loan at 6% per annum: A partner who advances a loan beyond agreed capital gets 6% p.a. (ii) No salary or commission to any partner: Partners are not entitled to remuneration.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) A partner who advances a loan beyond agreed capital gets 6% p.a. (ii) Partners are not entitled to remuneration.

items.stem: There is no partnership deed between Mehak and Karthik. Mehak gave the firm a loan of ₹60,000 on 1 July 2025. Interest on the loan for the year ended 31 March 2026 will be:
items.markingKey: (a) 6% p.a. for 9 months = ₹2,700.

items.stem: Rahul and Diya are partners without a partnership deed. On 1 October 2025 Rahul advanced a loan of ₹1,80,000 to the firm. The profit for the year ended 31 March 2026, before any interest on the loan, was ₹66,000. Calculate the interest on the loan and each partner's share of profit.
items.answer: Interest on loan ₹5,400; profit ₹60,600, ₹30,300 each
items.markingKey: Interest at 6% p.a. for 6 months: ₹1,80,000 × 6/100 × 6/12 = ₹5,400 (1 mark; a charge, allowed even if it creates a loss). Balance ₹66,000 − ₹5,400 = profit ₹60,600 shared equally, ₹30,300 each (2 marks).

items.stem: Meera and Dev are partners without a partnership deed. On 1 January 2025 Meera advanced a loan of ₹1,00,000 to the firm. The profit for the year ended 31 March 2026, before any interest on the loan, was ₹1,20,000. Calculate the interest on the loan and each partner's share of profit.
items.answer: Interest on loan ₹1,500; profit ₹1,18,500, ₹59,250 each
items.markingKey: Interest at 6% p.a. for 3 months: ₹1,00,000 × 6/100 × 3/12 = ₹1,500 (1 mark; a charge, allowed even if it creates a loss). Balance ₹1,20,000 − ₹1,500 = profit ₹1,18,500 shared equally, ₹59,250 each (2 marks).

items.stem: Which partnership term is described here? "The liability of partners for the debts of the firm extends to their private assets."
items.answer: Unlimited liability
items.markingKey: (a) Unlimited liability: The liability of partners for the debts of the firm extends to their private assets.
options: Unlimited liability
Firm name
Mutual agency
Firm

items.stem: Aditi, Varun and Sahil have no partnership deed. Aditi works full-time and claims a salary of ₹20,000 a month. Under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (no partnership deed), is the claim valid? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Not valid. No salary is allowed to a partner without a deed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Not valid; 2 marks for the justification: No salary is allowed to a partner without a deed.

items.stem: There is no partnership deed between Pooja and Gauri. Pooja gave the firm a loan of ₹2,60,000 on 1 January 2025. Interest on the loan for the year ended 31 March 2026 will be:
items.markingKey: (b) 6% p.a. for 3 months = ₹3,900.

items.stem:
Arjun and Gauri are partners. A dispute arose because nothing was written down about interest on capital, drawings and salary. A friend advises them to draw up a partnership deed.
(i) State four matters the deed should contain. (ii) Why is a written deed better than an oral agreement?
items.answer: (i) Capital of each partner; profit-sharing ratio; interest on capital and drawings; salary or commission; rules for admission and retirement (any four). (ii) It is evidence of the terms, avoids disputes, and must be stamped and can be registered.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Capital of each partner; profit-sharing ratio; interest on capital and drawings; salary or commission; rules for admission and retirement (any four). (ii) It is evidence of the terms, avoids disputes, and must be stamped and can be registered.

items.stem: What is meant by "Firm"?
items.answer: Persons who have entered into partnership with one another are collectively called this.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Persons who have entered into partnership with one another are collectively called this.

items.stem:
Aditya, Harleen and Kabir started a firm in Guwahati without a partnership deed. Aditya contributed ₹3,00,000, Harleen ₹2,00,000 and Kabir ₹1,00,000. Kabir also gave the firm a loan of ₹60,000. At the year end Aditya wants profits shared in the capital ratio and Harleen, who works full-time, wants a salary.
(i) How will profit be shared and are the two demands valid? (ii) What is Kabir entitled to on the loan for a full year?
items.answer: (i) Equally; neither demand is valid without a deed (no capital-ratio sharing, no salary). (ii) Interest at 6% p.a.: ₹3,600, a charge against profit.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Equally; neither demand is valid without a deed (no capital-ratio sharing, no salary). (ii) Interest at 6% p.a.: ₹3,600, a charge against profit.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Fixed capital method"?
items.answer: The method under which partners' capitals remain unchanged unless capital is added or withdrawn by agreement, and adjustments go to current accounts.
items.markingKey: (a) Fixed capital method: The method under which partners' capitals remain unchanged unless capital is added or withdrawn by agreement, and adjustments go to current accounts.
options: The method under which partners' capitals remain unchanged unless capital is added or withdrawn by agreement, and adjustments go to current accounts.
The account, kept under the fixed capital method, to which interest on capital, salary, drawings, interest on drawings and share of profit are posted.
The method under which all adjustments such as interest, salary, drawings and share of profit are recorded in a single capital account of each partner.
Money or goods withdrawn by a partner from the firm for personal use.

items.stem: State one difference between the fixed capital method and the fluctuating capital method on the basis of balance.
items.answer: the fixed capital method: capital account always shows a credit balance; the fluctuating capital method: capital account may show a debit balance
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the fixed capital method: capital account always shows a credit balance; the fluctuating capital method: capital account may show a debit balance

items.stem: Distinguish between the fixed capital method and the fluctuating capital method on the basis of balance, change in capital and number of accounts.
items.answer: (i) Balance: the fixed capital method: capital account always shows a credit balance; the fluctuating capital method: capital account may show a debit balance. (ii) Change in capital: the fixed capital method: capital remains unchanged except for additional capital or withdrawal of capital; the fluctuating capital method: capital changes every year. (iii) Number of accounts: the fixed capital method: two accounts (capital and current) for each partner; the fluctuating capital method: only one account (capital) for each partner.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Balance: the fixed capital method: capital account always shows a credit balance; the fluctuating capital method: capital account may show a debit balance. (ii) Change in capital: the fixed capital method: capital remains unchanged except for additional capital or withdrawal of capital; the fluctuating capital method: capital changes every year. (iii) Number of accounts: the fixed capital method: two accounts (capital and current) for each partner; the fluctuating capital method: only one account (capital) for each partner.

items.stem: Under the fluctuating capital method, Kunal's capital on 1 April 2025 was ₹4,60,000. During the year ended 31 March 2026: interest on capital @ 6% p.a., salary ₹48,000, share of profit ₹54,000, drawings ₹33,600 and interest on drawings ₹2,200. Find Kunal's capital on 31 March 2026.
items.markingKey: ₹4,60,000 + interest on capital ₹27,600 + salary ₹48,000 + profit ₹54,000 − drawings ₹33,600 − interest on drawings ₹2,200 = ₹5,53,800 (credits 1½, debits 1½).

items.stem: Pooja's fixed capital is ₹4,20,000 and Pooja's current account had a credit balance of ₹15,000 on 1 April 2025. For the year ended 31 March 2026: interest on capital @ 12% p.a., salary ₹18,000, share of profit ₹1,15,000, drawings ₹54,000, interest on drawings ₹2,700. Find the balance of the current account on 31 March 2026 and the capital account balance.
items.answer: Current account credit balance ₹1,41,700; capital account stays ₹4,20,000
items.markingKey: Current account: +₹15,000 + ₹50,400 interest + ₹18,000 salary + ₹1,15,000 profit − ₹54,000 drawings − ₹2,700 interest on drawings = credit ₹1,41,700 (2 marks). Fixed capital unchanged at ₹4,20,000 (1 mark).

items.stem: Saanvi's fixed capital is ₹1,60,000 and Saanvi's current account had a debit balance of ₹11,000 on 1 April 2025. For the year ended 31 March 2026: interest on capital @ 10% p.a., share of profit ₹1,41,000, drawings ₹12,000, interest on drawings ₹2,700. Find the balance of the current account on 31 March 2026 and the capital account balance.
items.answer: Current account credit balance ₹1,31,300; capital account stays ₹1,60,000
items.markingKey: Current account: −₹11,000 + ₹16,000 interest + ₹1,41,000 profit − ₹12,000 drawings − ₹2,700 interest on drawings = credit ₹1,31,300 (2 marks). Fixed capital unchanged at ₹1,60,000 (1 mark).

items.stem: Under the fluctuating capital method, Ishita's capital on 1 April 2025 was ₹4,90,000. During the year ended 31 March 2026: interest on capital @ 8% p.a., salary ₹12,000, share of profit ₹1,23,000, drawings ₹48,000 and interest on drawings ₹2,700. Find Ishita's capital on 31 March 2026.
items.markingKey: ₹4,90,000 + interest on capital ₹39,200 + salary ₹12,000 + profit ₹1,23,000 − drawings ₹48,000 − interest on drawings ₹2,700 = ₹6,13,500 (credits 1½, debits 1½).

items.stem: Which of the following is true of the fixed capital method but not of the fluctuating capital method?
items.answer: Provision in deed: must be specifically provided in the deed
items.markingKey: (d) the fixed capital method: Provision in deed: must be specifically provided in the deed. The other options describe the fluctuating capital method.
options: Number of accounts: only one account (capital) for each partner
Provision in deed: followed when the deed is silent
Adjustments: all adjustments are posted to the capital accounts
Provision in deed: must be specifically provided in the deed

items.stem: Shreya withdrew ₹5,000 every month for personal use. Under the fixed capital method, which account will the item be posted to? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Partner's Current Account. Drawings are debited to the current account.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Partner's Current Account; 2 marks for the justification: Drawings are debited to the current account.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the methods of maintaining partners' capital accounts is correct?
items.answer: Under the fluctuating capital method there is only one account for each partner.
items.markingKey: (b) Correct: Under the fluctuating capital method there is only one account for each partner.
options: Under the fixed capital method drawings are debited to the capital account.
Under the fluctuating capital method there is only one account for each partner.
Interest on capital is credited to the profit and loss account.
Under the fluctuating capital method each partner has a current account too.

items.stem: Imran's fixed capital is ₹4,50,000 and Imran's current account had a debit balance of ₹40,000 on 1 April 2025. For the year ended 31 March 2026: interest on capital @ 6% p.a., share of profit ₹1,49,000, drawings ₹33,600, interest on drawings ₹2,300. Find the balance of the current account on 31 March 2026 and the capital account balance.
items.answer: Current account credit balance ₹1,00,100; capital account stays ₹4,50,000
items.markingKey: Current account: −₹40,000 + ₹27,000 interest + ₹1,49,000 profit − ₹33,600 drawings − ₹2,300 interest on drawings = credit ₹1,00,100 (2 marks). Fixed capital unchanged at ₹4,50,000 (1 mark).

items.stem: What is meant by "Drawings"?
items.answer: Money or goods withdrawn by a partner from the firm for personal use.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Money or goods withdrawn by a partner from the firm for personal use.

items.stem: What is meant by "Divisible profit"?
items.answer: The balance of the profit and loss appropriation account shared among partners in their profit-sharing ratio.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The balance of the profit and loss appropriation account shared among partners in their profit-sharing ratio.

items.stem: Priya, a partner, is entitled to a commission of 4% of the net profit after charging such commission. The net profit before commission is ₹2,60,000. Priya's commission is:
items.markingKey: (b) Commission = profit × 4/104 = ₹10,000.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the profit and loss appropriation account is NOT correct?
items.answer: It is prepared to find the net profit of the firm.
items.markingKey: (d) Incorrect statement: It is prepared to find the net profit of the firm.
options: Interest on drawings is shown on its credit side.
Partner's salary and commission are shown on its debit side.
It is an extension of the profit and loss account.
It is prepared to find the net profit of the firm.

items.stem: Transfer of 10% of profit to general reserve. Where is the item shown?
items.answer: Debit of Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c
items.markingKey: (a) Debit of Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c. Transfer to reserve is an appropriation.
options: Debit of Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c
Credit of Profit and Loss A/c
Debit of Profit and Loss A/c
Credit of Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c

items.stem: Transfer of 10% of profit to general reserve. Where is the item shown? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Debit of Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c. Transfer to reserve is an appropriation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Debit of Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c; 2 marks for the justification: Transfer to reserve is an appropriation.

items.stem: Dev, Priya and Nandini are partners sharing profits in the ratio 2:2:1. Their capitals on 1 April 2025 were Dev ₹4,20,000, Priya ₹2,20,000, Nandini ₹4,60,000. The deed provides: interest on capital @ 8% p.a.; salary to Dev ₹8,000 per month; commission to Nandini @ 2% of the net profit (before charging commission). Interest on drawings: Dev ₹3,100, Priya ₹2,000, Nandini ₹1,500. The net profit for the year ended 31 March 2026 was ₹8,43,000. Prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account.
items.answer: Divisible profit ₹6,48,740: Dev ₹2,59,496, Priya ₹2,59,496, Nandini ₹1,29,748
items.markingKey: Credit: net profit ₹8,43,000 + interest on drawings ₹6,600 = ₹8,49,600. Debit: interest on capital Dev ₹33,600, Priya ₹17,600, Nandini ₹36,800; salary to Dev ₹96,000; commission to Nandini ₹16,860. Divisible profit ₹6,48,740 shared 2:2:1: Dev ₹2,59,496, Priya ₹2,59,496, Nandini ₹1,29,748. (1 mark each: interest on capital, salary/commission, interest on drawings, divisible profit; 2 marks for shares.)

items.stem: Sneha and Ishaan are partners sharing profits in the ratio 2:3. Their capitals were Sneha ₹4,20,000, Ishaan ₹4,20,000. The deed allows interest on capital @ 10% p.a. The net profit for the year ended 31 March 2026 is ₹41,500. Show the distribution of profit.
items.answer: Sneha ₹20,750; Ishaan ₹20,750 (profit distributed in the ratio of interest on capital)
items.markingKey: Interest on capital due: Sneha ₹42,000, Ishaan ₹42,000 = ₹84,000, which exceeds the profit ₹41,500. Interest on capital is allowed only out of profit, so the profit is distributed in the ratio of interest due (1:1): Sneha ₹20,750, Ishaan ₹20,750. No profit is left for sharing in the profit-sharing ratio.

items.stem: Varun, Dev and Mehak are partners sharing profits in the ratio 5:4:1. Their capitals on 1 April 2025 were Varun ₹2,60,000, Dev ₹3,20,000, Mehak ₹2,20,000. The deed provides: interest on capital @ 8% p.a.; salary to Dev ₹14,000 per month; commission to Mehak @ 5% of the net profit (before charging commission). Interest on drawings: Varun ₹3,300, Dev ₹1,100, Mehak ₹900. The net profit for the year ended 31 March 2026 was ₹6,60,000. Prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account.
items.answer: Divisible profit ₹4,00,300: Varun ₹2,00,150, Dev ₹1,60,120, Mehak ₹40,030
items.markingKey: Credit: net profit ₹6,60,000 + interest on drawings ₹5,300 = ₹6,65,300. Debit: interest on capital Varun ₹20,800, Dev ₹25,600, Mehak ₹17,600; salary to Dev ₹1,68,000; commission to Mehak ₹33,000. Divisible profit ₹4,00,300 shared 5:4:1: Varun ₹2,00,150, Dev ₹1,60,120, Mehak ₹40,030. (1 mark each: interest on capital, salary/commission, interest on drawings, divisible profit; 2 marks for shares.)

items.stem: Kabir and Rohan are partners sharing profits in the ratio 7:3. Their capitals were Kabir ₹2,00,000, Rohan ₹4,00,000. The deed allows interest on capital @ 6% p.a. The net profit for the year ended 31 March 2026 is ₹13,500. Show the distribution of profit.
items.answer: Kabir ₹4,500; Rohan ₹9,000 (profit distributed in the ratio of interest on capital)
items.markingKey: Interest on capital due: Kabir ₹12,000, Rohan ₹24,000 = ₹36,000, which exceeds the profit ₹13,500. Interest on capital is allowed only out of profit, so the profit is distributed in the ratio of interest due (1:2): Kabir ₹4,500, Rohan ₹9,000. No profit is left for sharing in the profit-sharing ratio.

items.stem: Where is the item shown? In each case give a reason. (i) Interest charged on Siddharth's drawings. (ii) Transfer of 10% of profit to general reserve.
items.answer: (i) Credit of Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c: Interest on drawings is a gain to the firm, credited to the appropriation account. (ii) Debit of Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c: Transfer to reserve is an appropriation.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Credit of Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c (ii) Debit of Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the profit and loss appropriation account is correct?
items.answer: It is an extension of the profit and loss account.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: It is an extension of the profit and loss account.
options: Interest on capital is shown on its credit side.
Rent paid to a partner is shown on its debit side.
It is an extension of the profit and loss account.
Interest on a partner's loan is shown on its debit side.

items.stem: Priya made the following drawings during the year ended 31 March 2026: 1 July 2025 ₹21,000; 1 November 2025 ₹10,000; 1 February 2026 ₹12,000; 1 March 2026 ₹25,000. Calculate interest on drawings @ 10% p.a. using the product method.
Nikhil's capital on 1 April 2025 was ₹4,40,000. Nikhil introduced additional capital of ₹24,000 on 1 July 2025. Calculate interest on capital @ 6% p.a. for the year ended 31 March 2026.
Sahil, a partner, withdrew ₹16,000 at the beginning of every quarter during the year ended 31 March 2026. Calculate interest on drawings @ 8% p.a.
items.markingKey: Total drawings ₹64,000; average period 7.5 months; ₹64,000 × 8/100 × 7.5/12 = ₹3,200.

items.stem: Aisha, a partner, withdrew ₹8,000 at the beginning of every quarter during the year ended 31 March 2026. Calculate interest on drawings @ 9% p.a.
items.markingKey: (a) Total drawings ₹32,000; average period 7.5 months; ₹32,000 × 9/100 × 7.5/12 = ₹1,800.

items.stem: What is meant by "Adjustment entry"?
items.answer: A single journal entry passed through partners' capital or current accounts to correct an omission without reopening the closed accounts.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A single journal entry passed through partners' capital or current accounts to correct an omission without reopening the closed accounts.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about guarantee of profit and past adjustments is correct?
items.answer: If the guaranteed partner's share exceeds the guaranteed amount, no deficiency arises.
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: If the guaranteed partner's share exceeds the guaranteed amount, no deficiency arises.
options: If the guaranteed partner's share exceeds the guaranteed amount, no deficiency arises.
A guarantee is a charge against profit.
Deficiency is always borne equally by all partners.
A guaranteed partner always gets exactly the guaranteed amount.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about guarantee of profit and past adjustments is NOT correct?
items.answer: Deficiency is always borne equally by all partners.
items.markingKey: (c) Incorrect statement: Deficiency is always borne equally by all partners.
options: Past adjustments do not reopen the closed profit and loss account.
If the guaranteed partner's share exceeds the guaranteed amount, no deficiency arises.
Deficiency is always borne equally by all partners.
A guarantee may be given by one partner or by the firm.

items.stem: Harpreet, Farhan and Ishaan share profits 3:3:2. Ishaan is guaranteed a minimum profit of ₹59,500. If the firm's profit is ₹1,74,000, the deficiency to be made good is:

Om, Rohan and Mehak share profits in the ratio 5:4:1. Om guaranteed Mehak a minimum profit of ₹9,600, any deficiency to be borne by Om. The profit for the year ended 31 March 2026 is ₹66,000. Show the distribution of profit.
items.markingKey: Shares 5:4:1: Om ₹33,000, Rohan ₹26,400, Mehak ₹6,600. Deficiency of Mehak ₹9,600 − ₹6,600 = ₹3,000, borne by Om alone. Final: Om ₹30,000, Rohan ₹26,400, Mehak ₹9,600.

items.stem: Aarav, Imran and Kabir were partners sharing profits 3:3:2, with fixed capitals Aarav ₹1,40,000, Imran ₹1,10,000, Kabir ₹1,70,000. After the accounts for the year ended 31 March 2026 were closed, it was found that interest on capital @ 6% p.a. had been omitted. Pass the adjustment entry.
items.answer: Aarav's Capital A/c Dr ₹1,050; Imran's Capital A/c Dr ₹2,850; To Kabir's Capital A/c ₹3,900
items.markingKey: Interest due: Aarav ₹8,400, Imran ₹6,600, Kabir ₹10,200 (total ₹25,200). Borne in profit ratio: Aarav ₹9,450, Imran ₹9,450, Kabir ₹6,300. Net: Aarav −₹1,050, Imran −₹2,850, Kabir +₹3,900. Entry: Aarav's Capital A/c Dr ₹1,050; Imran's Capital A/c Dr ₹2,850; To Kabir's Capital A/c ₹3,900. (Capitals are fixed, so current accounts may be used instead of capital accounts.)

items.stem: Meera, Sahil and Aditya share profits 3:3:2. Aditya is guaranteed a minimum profit of ₹76,500. If the firm's profit is ₹2,46,000, the deficiency to be made good is:

Lakshmi, Meera and Imran share profits in the ratio 5:4:1. Meera guaranteed Imran a minimum profit of ₹39,000, any deficiency to be borne by Meera. The profit for the year ended 31 March 2026 is ₹3,00,000. Show the distribution of profit.
items.markingKey: Shares 5:4:1: Lakshmi ₹1,50,000, Meera ₹1,20,000, Imran ₹30,000. Deficiency of Imran ₹39,000 − ₹30,000 = ₹9,000, borne by Meera alone. Final: Lakshmi ₹1,50,000, Meera ₹1,11,000, Imran ₹39,000.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Past adjustments"?
items.answer: Corrections made after the final accounts are closed for omissions or errors such as interest on capital or salary not recorded.
items.markingKey: (a) Past adjustments: Corrections made after the final accounts are closed for omissions or errors such as interest on capital or salary not recorded.
options: Corrections made after the final accounts are closed for omissions or errors such as interest on capital or salary not recorded.
An assurance that a partner will receive a minimum amount of profit, any deficiency being borne by the guaranteeing partner or partners.
A single journal entry passed through partners' capital or current accounts to correct an omission without reopening the closed accounts.
The amount by which a partner's actual share of profit falls short of the guaranteed minimum.

items.stem: Aditya, Gauri and Arjun share profits 1:1:1. Aditya is guaranteed a minimum profit of ₹94,000. If the firm's profit is ₹2,40,000, the deficiency to be made good is:

Assertion (A): If interest on capital was omitted, the partner with the highest capital always gains on adjustment.
Reason (R): Adjustment compares interest due with the share of that amount borne in the profit ratio.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: the gain depends on capital relative to profit share, not capital alone. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Saanvi was credited with a salary of ₹12,000 a month. Under the fixed capital method, which account will the item be posted to?
items.answer: Partner's Current Account
items.markingKey: (c) Partner's Current Account. Salary is credited to the current account.
options: Profit and Loss Account
Profit and Loss Appropriation Account
Partner's Current Account
Partner's Capital Account

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the provisions applicable in the absence of a partnership deed is NOT correct?
items.answer: Profits are shared in the capital ratio.
items.markingKey: (a) Incorrect statement: Profits are shared in the capital ratio.
options: Profits are shared in the capital ratio.
Profits and losses are shared equally.
No interest is allowed on partners' capitals.
No partner is entitled to a salary.

items.stem: Nikhil and Fatima are partners sharing profits in the ratio 2:3. Their capitals on 1 April 2025 were Nikhil ₹1,60,000, Fatima ₹3,20,000. The deed provides: interest on capital @ 12% p.a.; salary to Nikhil ₹11,000 per month. Interest on drawings: Nikhil ₹2,500, Fatima ₹3,300. The net profit for the year ended 31 March 2026 was ₹4,43,000. Prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account.
items.answer: Divisible profit ₹2,59,200: Nikhil ₹1,03,680, Fatima ₹1,55,520
items.markingKey: Credit: net profit ₹4,43,000 + interest on drawings ₹5,800 = ₹4,48,800. Debit: interest on capital Nikhil ₹19,200, Fatima ₹38,400; salary to Nikhil ₹1,32,000. items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Interest on drawings"?
items.answer: An amount charged to partners on money withdrawn, credited to the profit and loss appropriation account.
items.markingKey: (c) Interest on drawings: An amount charged to partners on money withdrawn, credited to the profit and loss appropriation account.
options: Calculating interest on drawings by multiplying each drawing by the months it was outstanding and charging interest on the total of products for one month.
An extension of the profit and loss account of a firm that shows how net profit is distributed among partners after interest, salary and commission.
An amount charged to partners on money withdrawn, credited to the profit and loss appropriation account.
The balance of the profit and loss appropriation account shared among partners in their profit-sharing ratio.

items.stem: Saanvi, Tanvi and Shreya share profits in the ratio 1:1:1. The firm guaranteed Saanvi a minimum profit of ₹42,000. The profit for the year ended 31 March 2026 is ₹1,08,000. Show the distribution of profit.
items.answer: Saanvi ₹42,000, Tanvi ₹33,000, Shreya ₹33,000
items.markingKey: Shares 1:1:1: Saanvi ₹36,000, Tanvi ₹36,000, Shreya ₹36,000. Deficiency of Saanvi ₹42,000 − ₹36,000 = ₹6,000, borne by the firm (deficiency borne by Tanvi and Shreya in their ratio 1:1). Final: Saanvi ₹42,000, Tanvi ₹33,000, Shreya ₹33,000.

items.stem: There is no partnership deed between Harleen and Nikhil. Harleen gave the firm a loan of ₹2,80,000 on 1 April 2025. Interest on the loan for the year ended 31 March 2026 will be:
items.markingKey: (b) 6% p.a. for 12 months = ₹16,800.

items.stem: Arjun advanced a loan of ₹1,00,000 to the firm of Arjun and Kunal. There is no deed. Arjun claims interest at 6% p.a. on the loan. Under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (no partnership deed), is the claim valid?
items.answer: Valid
items.markingKey: (c) Valid. Interest on a partner's loan is allowed at 6% p.a. even without a deed.
options: Not valid
Valid only with consent of all partners
Valid
Valid only if the firm earns a profit

items.stem: Arjun and Siddharth are partners sharing profits in the ratio 3:1. Their capitals were Arjun ₹4,60,000, Siddharth ₹1,40,000. The deed allows interest on capital @ 6% p.a. The net profit for the year ended 31 March 2026 is ₹24,000. Show the distribution of profit.
items.answer: Arjun ₹18,400; Siddharth ₹5,600 (profit distributed in the ratio of interest on capital)
items.markingKey: Interest on capital due: Arjun ₹27,600, Siddharth ₹8,400 = ₹36,000, which exceeds the profit ₹24,000. Interest on capital is allowed only out of profit, so the profit is distributed in the ratio of interest due (23:7): Arjun ₹18,400, Siddharth ₹5,600. No profit is left for sharing in the profit-sharing ratio.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 that apply in the absence of a partnership deed?
items.answer: Salary or commission to partners
items.markingKey: (b) "Salary or commission to partners" is one of the contents of a partnership deed, not one of the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 that apply in the absence of a partnership deed.
options: Interest on a partner's loan at 6% per annum
Salary or commission to partners
No salary or commission to any partner
No interest on capital is allowed

items.stem: Sahil was credited with a salary of ₹12,000 a month. Under the fixed capital method, which account will the item be posted to? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Partner's Current Account. Salary is credited to the current account.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Partner's Current Account; 2 marks for the justification: Salary is credited to the current account.

items.stem: What is meant by "Guarantee of profit"?
items.answer: An assurance that a partner will receive a minimum amount of profit, any deficiency being borne by the guaranteeing partner or partners.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: An assurance that a partner will receive a minimum amount of profit, any deficiency being borne by the guaranteeing partner or partners.

items.stem:

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Under the fixed capital method, which account will the item be posted to? In each case give a reason. (i) Riya was credited with a salary of ₹12,000 a month. (ii) Riya permanently withdrew ₹40,000 of capital with the consent of all partners.
items.answer: (i) Partner's Current Account: Salary is credited to the current account. (ii) Partner's Capital Account: Withdrawal of capital reduces the fixed capital.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Partner's Current Account (ii) Partner's Capital Account

items.stem: Farhan and Tara are partners sharing profits in the ratio 7:3. Their capitals were Farhan ₹2,40,000, Tara ₹2,40,000. The deed allows interest on capital @ 5% p.a. The net profit for the year ended 31 March 2026 is ₹23,000. Show the distribution of profit.
items.answer: Farhan ₹11,500; Tara ₹11,500 (profit distributed in the ratio of interest on capital)
items.markingKey: Interest on capital due: Farhan ₹12,000, Tara ₹12,000 = ₹24,000, which exceeds the profit ₹23,000. Interest on capital is allowed only out of profit, so the profit is distributed in the ratio of interest due (1:1): Farhan ₹11,500, Tara ₹11,500. No profit is left for sharing in the profit-sharing ratio.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the contents of a partnership deed?
items.answer: Profits and losses are shared equally

Names and addresses of the firm and partners
Method of settling disputes
Capital contributed by each partner

items.stem: Farhan withdrew ₹5,000 every month for personal use. Under the fixed capital method, which account will the item be posted to?
items.answer: Partner's Current Account

Partner's Current Account

items.answer: Interest on drawings is charged at 6% per annum.

options: No partner is entitled to a salary.

items.stem: Aryan, Farhan and Ananya are partners sharing profits in the ratio 5:3:2. Their capitals on 1 April 2025 were Aryan ₹3,80,000, Farhan ₹4,20,000, Ananya ₹1,00,000. Interest on drawings: Aryan ₹2,500, Farhan ₹2,300, Ananya ₹3,000. The net profit for the year ended 31 March 2026 was ₹6,98,000. Prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account.
items.answer: Divisible profit ₹5,20,900: Aryan ₹2,60,450, Farhan ₹1,56,270, Ananya ₹1,04,180
items.markingKey: Credit: net profit ₹6,98,000 + interest on drawings ₹7,800 = ₹7,05,800. Debit: interest on capital Aryan ₹38,000, Farhan ₹42,000, Ananya ₹10,000; salary to Farhan ₹60,000; commission to Farhan ₹34,900. (1 mark each: interest on capital, salary/commission, interest on drawings, divisible profit; 2 marks for shares.)

items.stem: Lakshmi, Diya and Tara share profits in the ratio 5:3:2. Diya guaranteed Lakshmi a minimum profit of ₹1,01,000, any deficiency to be borne by Diya. The profit for the year ended 31 March 2026 is ₹1,86,000. Show the distribution of profit.

items.answer: Corrections made after the final accounts are closed for omissions or errors such as interest on capital or salary not recorded.
